nodes.label: AGENTS.md Entry Point
nodes.rationale: One tool-agnostic file is the single source of truth so rules never drift between Claude, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Aider, Continue and Zed; tool-specific files are pointers only.

nodes.label: ShowHow
nodes.rationale: Offline Android app: one narrated take in Hindi or Marathi becomes a step-by-step guide (one photo + one audio slice per step) runnable hands-free. Everything on-device so nothing leaves the phone.

nodes.label: iQOO City Battles 2026
nodes.rationale: 30-hour hackathon, three-person team — the deadline and jury are why the four constraints are product claims rather than preferences.

nodes.label: The Four Hard Constraints
nodes.rationale: These are claims made to a jury; breaking one is worse than shipping less, so none may be 'temporarily' relaxed.

nodes.label: No INTERNET Permission
nodes.rationale: Manifest declares only CAMERA and RECORD_AUDIO and strips INTERNET, ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE and WAKE_LOCK with tools:node="remove" in case a dependency merges them in. The strip exists because the offline claim must survive manifest merge, and the app-info screen proves it to a jury in four seconds.

nodes.label: Step Cutter Is A Pause Detector Plus A Word List
nodes.rationale: No video model and no ML anywhere in that path, because it must run on a five-year-old phone.
nodes.norm_label: step cutter is a pause detector plus a word list

nodes.label: Mode Engine Contains No AI
nodes.rationale: Plain rules over four booleans so the decision lands in well under 10 ms and is explainable.

nodes.label: Warnings Advise, They Never Block
nodes.rationale: There is no disabled button anywhere. Anything the phone cannot honestly measure (gloves, driving, age, whether the work is correct) is a user setting, never a guess — a wrong guess that blocks the user is worse than no guess.

nodes.label: core/ Is Pure Kotlin With Zero android.* Imports
nodes.rationale: Purity keeps the core logic JVM-testable in seconds (./gradlew test), which is the only fast feedback loop available during the no-compile Red Light windows. Checked with grep -rn '^import android' over core/.
nodes.norm_label: core/ is pure kotlin with zero android.* imports

nodes.label: Invariant Check Table
nodes.rationale: Every invariant is paired with a runnable check (grep over the merged manifest, PolicyStoreTest, StepCutterTest, ./gradlew test) so an agent can verify rather than assert.

nodes.label: Live Policy Retune Without Compiling
nodes.rationale: On first run the app copies assets/policy.json into filesDir/policy.json and thereafter reads only that file, watching the DIRECTORY with a FileObserver — editors and adb replace the inode, so a watch on the file itself would die. adb push retunes live with no restart. A malformed file is logged and ignored so the last good policy stays in force and tuning is never reset.

nodes.label: Red Light (No-Compile Window)
nodes.rationale: For roughly 10.5 hours of the event nobody can compile; the only compile windows are Sat 11:00-13:00, Sat 15:30-16:30 and Sun 01:00-06:30. This is why no behaviour may be hardcoded.

nodes.label: Every Tunable Number Lives In Policy
nodes.rationale: A new knob must be added in BOTH core/Policy.kt and app/src/main/assets/policy.json, or the team cannot tune it during Red Light.
nodes.norm_label: every tunable number lives in policy

nodes.label: One File, One Owner
nodes.rationale: Git conflicts happen when two people edit the same file, so no two people ever edit the same file. An agent inherits the ownership of whoever drives it; if a change belongs in someone else's folder it must stop and say so.

nodes.label: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: Owns core/, capture/, ai/, data/, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and — exclusively — build.gradle.kts, AndroidManifest.xml and gradle/libs.versions.toml.

nodes.label: Anushka
nodes.rationale: Owns every Compose screen, theme and all visuals under ui/.

nodes.label: Ayaan
nodes.rationale: Owns app/src/main/assets/policy.json (every tunable number and both word lists) plus docs/ and README.md, except docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

nodes.label: AdaptiveGate
nodes.rationale: Tracks the room's noise floor so a fixed dB threshold cannot fail in a fan-noise kitchen. Also eats -Infinity/NaN from a dead mic.

nodes.label: StepCutter
nodes.rationale: Silence runs >= pauseMs become cuts at the pause midpoint; short utterances merge forward; hard cap at maxSteps. Step ranges must tile the take exactly — no gaps, no overlaps (StepCutterTest).

nodes.label: ModeEngine
nodes.rationale: Picks EASY/HANDS/TALK/TAP from four booleans using Schmitt triggers plus a dwell timer so the mode cannot flicker. Its output currently changes nothing outside the Debug screen.

nodes.label: SceneHash
nodes.rationale: 64-bit dHash (70%) blended with an HSV histogram (30%) — deliberately no model file, so scene comparison costs nothing and ships no weights.

nodes.label: Policy
nodes.rationale: The single Kotlin home for every tunable number, mirrored by app/src/main/assets/policy.json.

nodes.label: PolicyStore
nodes.rationale: Guarded by PolicyStoreTest: a malformed policy.json never crashes and never resets tuning.

nodes.label: GuideStore
nodes.rationale: Plain folders on disk — no database, matching the offline, zero-dependency posture.

nodes.label: LinkWordConfirmer
nodes.rationale: Currently a no-op and ShowHowViewModel does not pass it to StepCutter, so the 'word list' half of constraint 2 is unimplemented and the pause detector stands alone.

nodes.label: RealSceneCheck
nodes.rationale: Written and correct but unwired — ShowScreen binds the camera with analyzer = null.

nodes.label: FakeAsr / FakeCaptioner / FakeGestureSource
nodes.rationale: Return canned data. vosk-android, mediapipe-tasks-* and onnxruntime are declared in gradle/libs.versions.toml but never imported — they still cost 121 MB of APK.

nodes.label: ShowHowViewModel
nodes.rationale: Hardcodes speechUnclear and userFar to false and guide language to "hi", which leaves linkWordsMr dead.

nodes.label: Photo/Step Index Mismatch Bug
nodes.rationale: Photos are indexed by shots++ from LIVE cut detection, but steps are indexed by the FINAL cut ranges after mergeShort and the maxSteps cap — so a photo can land on the wrong step. Documented under 'Known defects' in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

nodes.label: House Style
nodes.rationale: Boring over clever, shortest working diff, delete before you add. Comments explain WHY a number or branch exists, not what the line does. New non-trivial core/ logic gets a JVM test; UI does not. Never add a dependency for something a few lines can do — the APK is already 121 MB from unused ML libraries.

nodes.label: ponytail: Comment Convention
nodes.rationale: A deliberate shortcut with a known ceiling is marked with a ponytail: comment naming the ceiling and the upgrade path, so the shortcut is tracked instead of forgotten. AdaptiveGate and StepCutter already do this.

nodes.label: Git Rules
nodes.rationale: Work on main; pull before push; commit every 30-60 min; never force-push; never commit a model file (.task, .onnx, .tflite, .gguf, **/models/ are gitignored); only push code that builds, verified by ./gradlew test.

nodes.label: ./gradlew test
nodes.rationale: Runs the core logic on the JVM in seconds and is meant to be run constantly — the fast loop that makes Red Light survivable.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md Pointer
nodes.rationale: Exists only so Claude Code auto-loads something; the real, tool-agnostic instructions stay in AGENTS.md so they never fork per tool.

nodes.label: Role To Subagent Mapping
nodes.rationale: Maps each owned path set to a named subagent (core-systems, ai-integration, ui-compose, policy-tuning, demo-pitch, build-verify) so picking a role also picks the file boundary.

nodes.label: Two Claims Worth Re-Checking
nodes.rationale: Whenever a dependency changes, re-grep the merged manifest for surviving network permissions and re-grep core/ for android imports — a new dependency is the realistic way both claims silently break.

nodes.label: JDK 17+ Build Requirement
nodes.rationale: Verified on Temurin 25 and Android Studio's bundled JBR 21. local.properties is gitignored because sdk.dir is per-machine.

nodes.label: Copilot Instructions Pointer
nodes.rationale: A pointer only, so the rules stay in one place for every agent rather than being duplicated per tool.

nodes.label: Role Agents
nodes.rationale: Six role definitions, plain Markdown with a small YAML header and nothing Claude-specific, so any coding agent (or a human reading them as a checklist) can use them.

nodes.label: core-systems Role
nodes.rationale: Pure logic, capture and storage (Kshitij); writes core/, capture/, data/, app/src/test/.

nodes.label: ai-integration Role
nodes.rationale: Replaces the fakes with real models (Kshitij); writes ai/ plus the single wiring line in the ViewModel — the narrow write scope is what keeps the swap from touching anyone else's files.

nodes.label: ui-compose Role
nodes.rationale: Every screen the judge touches (Anushka); writes ui/ only.

nodes.label: policy-tuning Role
nodes.rationale: Tunes behaviour without compiling (Ayaan); writes app/src/main/assets/policy.json only.

nodes.label: demo-pitch Role
nodes.rationale: Runbook, Office Kit log and pitch (Ayaan); writes docs/ but not docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

nodes.label: build-verify Role
nodes.rationale: The gate before any push (Kshitij); writes nothing — read-only, reports. Owning no files is deliberate so the verifier cannot be tempted to fix what it finds.

nodes.label: Stay Inside Your Paths
nodes.rationale: The whole git strategy is that no two people edit the same file; if a fix belongs in someone else's folder, say so and stop rather than making it.

nodes.label: Report Honestly
nodes.rationale: If a test fails, say so with the output; if part of the task was skipped, say which part and why — under a 30-hour deadline a false green is more expensive than an admitted gap.

nodes.label: Cross-Tool Usage Of Role Files
nodes.rationale: Claude Code gets thin stubs in .claude/agents/ that point here; Cursor/Windsurf/Zed/Continue paste the body into a rules panel; Codex/Copilot/Aider open with 'Read AGENTS.md and agents/<role>.md'. Keeping the body tool-neutral means one edit updates every tool.

nodes.label: Show Mode
nodes.rationale: One continuous audio take with silences as step boundaries means the expert never stops working to author anything; the guide is a by-product of doing the job once.

nodes.label: Guide Mode
nodes.rationale: The follower has full hands, so the phone reads the room and picks how to help; the user never chooses a mode because choosing is itself an interaction they cannot afford.

nodes.label: Android-Free Core Package
nodes.rationale: core/ forbids any android.* import not for tidiness but so that 'a room floored at -20 dB by a ceiling fan' is a JVM test running in milliseconds instead of a trip to a real kitchen with a real fan.

nodes.label: Recording Data Flow
nodes.rationale: Mic -> 20 ms hops -> dBFS levels -> onLevel at 50 calls a second -> sample log -> stopRecording -> buildGuide. The sample log is the authoritative record; everything downstream replays it.

nodes.label: Two-Pass Cut Design
nodes.rationale: A cheap live pass exists only to decide when to take a photo; the authoritative pass runs once at the end over the whole sample log. They are allowed to disagree — that disagreement is defect #1.

nodes.label: Adaptive Gate
nodes.rationale: A fixed threshold cannot work: a ceiling fan floors a room around -20 dBFS and a gate nailed at -38 dB reads that as continuous speech, finds no pause, and returns the whole take as one enormous step. Tracking the floor instead is the only way the product survives a real workshop.

nodes.label: Asymmetric Noise-Floor Tracking
nodes.rationale: floorDb falls fast (gateFallCoef 0.25) so no priming special case is needed, rises slowly (gateRiseCoef 0.004) and is frozen while speech is present so a long sentence cannot drag the floor up behind it. -Infinity and NaN are sanitized to -120 before any arithmetic.

nodes.label: Step Cutter
nodes.rationale: Cuts land at the midpoint of a pause so the tail of one step and the run-up of the next both keep some air around them. Ranges must always tile the take, which is why everything past maxSteps lands in the final step rather than being discarded.

nodes.label: CutConfirmer
nodes.rationale: A veto/second-opinion seam so a smarter boundary check can be swapped in without changing the cutter; PassThroughConfirmer keeps it demoable today.

nodes.label: LinkWordConfirmer
nodes.rationale: Confirms a boundary where the expert actually said 'phir', 'uske baad', 'mag', 'tyanantar'. A no-op until ASR lands; the word lists already live in Policy so wiring it is a body change, not an API change.

nodes.label: mergeShort and maxSteps Cap
nodes.rationale: Dropping the boundary after a segment shorter than minUtteranceMs joins it forward; a short tail has no next, so the last boundary is dropped instead. Exact tiling is the invariant.

nodes.label: Mode Engine
nodes.rationale: Four modes with first-match-wins precedence: EASY (user setting, overrides everything), HANDS (loud room or unclear speech), TALK (phone flat or user far), TAP (held, quiet, close). A decision must land well inside 10 ms.

nodes.label: Schmitt-Trigger Hysteresis
nodes.rationale: inHand (accel variance) and roomLoud (dBFS) use enter thresholds different from exit thresholds so a value sitting on the line cannot flip.

nodes.label: Dwell Commit Delay
nodes.rationale: A candidate mode must survive dwellMs before commit; without it a borderline sample repaints the screen twice a second, and that flicker is exactly the problem the product exists to solve.

nodes.label: Mode Reason String
nodes.rationale: Every commit carries a human-readable reason such as 'HANDS <- room is loud (-24.3 dBFS)'. It is the honest-limits answer for the jury: the phone says why, it does not guess.

nodes.label: Policy Hot-Reload
nodes.rationale: The asset is a seed once — reading it again would make an override impossible. The FileObserver watches the directory, not the file, because editors and adb replace rather than modify and a watch on an inode dies with the inode. ignoreUnknownKeys keeps a hand-edited stray key from crashing; bad JSON keeps the previous good values.

nodes.label: On-Disk Guide Storage Format
nodes.rationale: Deliberately plain file IO, no Room and no DataStore: a guide you can drag from one phone to another with a file manager is the whole sharing story — no server, no export format. Photos are one-based on disk (s1 = index 0).

nodes.label: Sealed-Interface Navigation
nodes.rationale: The whole navigation graph is one `when` over a sealed interface. Navigation-Compose buys nothing for five screens and costs an argument about routes at 2 am.

nodes.label: ViewModel As The Only Layer Seam
nodes.rationale: ShowHowViewModel owns the recorder, motion flow, gate, engine, guide store and policy repo, and exposes one DebugState so the debug screen repaints atomically.
nodes.norm_label: viewmodel as the only layer seam

nodes.label: Photo-to-Step Index Mismatch
nodes.rationale: snap() names files by shots++ from live boundary detection while buildGuide assigns photoFile(id, r.index) from final ranges after mergeShort and the maxSteps cap. Live cuts >= final steps, so photos drift onto the wrong steps. Fix: record each snap timestamp and map snaps to ranges by time.

nodes.label: Fake AI Stack
nodes.rationale: Four interfaces (Asr, Captioner, GestureSource, SceneCheck) with canned implementations so the product is demoable with zero model files. FakeAsr returns nine canned Hindi words, FakeGestureSource emits OPEN_PALM into the void, FakeCaptioner cycles four strings, and RealSceneCheck is never called.

nodes.label: Declared-But-Unused ML Dependencies
nodes.source_location: §11 Dependencies declared but not yet used
nodes.rationale: mediapipe-tasks-vision, mediapipe-tasks-genai, onnxruntime-android and vosk-android are in the build tonight so APK size and manifest merge are known quantities before anyone is tired — which is also why the debug APK is 121 MB.

nodes.label: R8 Disabled In Release
nodes.rationale: R8 breaks MediaPipe, which stack-walks to load its native libraries. All three ML libraries ship their own libc++_shared.so, hence the pickFirsts in packaging.

nodes.label: File Ownership Rule
nodes.rationale: Git conflicts happen when two people edit the same file and almost nothing else causes them, so no two people ever edit the same file. Ten seconds of asking beats forty minutes of untangling. An agent inherits the ownership of whoever is driving it.

nodes.label: Commit Rhythm
nodes.rationale: Pull every time you sit down; add/commit/push every 30-60 minutes. Commit once every six hours and a crash costs six hours; commit every thirty minutes and it costs thirty.

nodes.label: Non-Negotiable Git Rules
nodes.rationale: Never force push (it deletes other people's work); never commit a model file (.task, .onnx, .tflite, .gguf, **/models/ are gitignored); only push code that builds, run ./gradlew test first; pull before you push.

nodes.label: Conflict Escape Hatch
nodes.rationale: Copy the changed file to the desktop, delete the folder, clone fresh, paste back, commit, push. Four minutes, crude, and has never once made things worse — chosen over teaching merge resolution at 3 am.

nodes.label: Work Directly On main
nodes.rationale: With file ownership in place, trunk-based work is safe and far faster than PRs nobody has time to review. Branch only for an experiment you might throw away.

nodes.label: Red Light
nodes.rationale: Roughly 10.5 hours with the laptop closed as a build machine. Red Light time is spent on policy.json tuning, phone testing, recording demo guides and pitch work.

nodes.label: Green Light Compile Windows
nodes.rationale: Sat 11:00-13:00 (models onto the phone), Sat 15:30-16:30 (whatever is genuinely broken, do not fill it in advance), Sun 01:00-06:30 (all heavy integration). Fifteen minutes before every Green window, decide out loud what gets compiled in it — Green time is the scarce resource.

nodes.label: Nothing May Be Hardcoded
nodes.rationale: During Red Light the only thing anyone can change is policy.json, pushed over Office Kit file transfer or adb. Every tunable therefore has to live in config, not in Kotlin.

nodes.label: Kshitij Desai
nodes.rationale: On-device AI and systems. Owns core/, capture/, ai/, data/, the build files and the manifest, plus the technical document and the answers to hard jury questions — nobody else can defend the adaptive gate.

nodes.label: Anushka Unde
nodes.rationale: UI/UX. Owns ui/ completely; Kshitij hands over plain working screens and she makes them worth looking at, carrying the deck's paper/black/blue visual language into the app so slides and product look like one thing.

nodes.label: Ayaan Memon
nodes.rationale: Office Kit, content, demo and pitch — the two scoring categories nobody else has time for. Five deliverables and nothing else is his job.

nodes.label: Screen Priority Order
nodes.rationale: PlayerScreen first (four visual states TAP/TALK/HANDS/EASY plus the mode reason bar; TALK readable across a room, HANDS usable with no touching at all), then ShowScreen, then ReviewScreen, then LibraryScreen — ordered by what the jury actually watches.

nodes.label: Office Kit Usage
nodes.rationale: Worth 10%, read off HackTracker device data — real counts and durations, so it cannot be faked on Sunday morning. Steady use across all 30 hours scores better than a burst at the end, logged one line per use in docs/officekit-log.md.

nodes.label: Hindi and Marathi Linking-Word Lists
nodes.rationale: Live inside policy.json so they are tunable during Red Light; they are the input that will make LinkWordConfirmer work once ASR lands.

nodes.label: Demo Runbook and Five Recorded Guides
nodes.rationale: End product quality is 30%, judged on a 2.5-minute live demo; the five guides recorded on Sunday morning are the insurance against a fumbled live recording.
nodes.norm_label: demo runbook and five recorded guides

nodes.label: Pitch Structure
nodes.rationale: Same five-beat shape every time: the problem in one sentence, Show Mode, Guide Mode, the honest part, the proof.

nodes.label: The Honest Part
nodes.rationale: State plainly what the team refuses to claim — gloves, driving, whether someone is elderly, whether the work is correct. Anything the phone cannot honestly measure is a setting, not a guess. Do not cut this point: a team that states its limits reads as more credible, not less.

nodes.label: No INTERNET Permission
nodes.rationale: The proof of the on-device claim, showable in the app info screen in four seconds.

nodes.label: Four-Hour Scope Check
nodes.rationale: Every four hours one person says out loud what the demo would look like if the team stopped right now; if the answer is 'nothing works', cut scope immediately, not at hour 28. Sleep in shifts — Ayaan pitches so Ayaan sleeps most.

nodes.label: Ownership Table
nodes.rationale: Rather than being clever about branching strategies, make sure no two people ever edit the same file. If a file is not in your list, you do not open it.

nodes.label: Five Git Commands
nodes.rationale: pull, add, commit, push, status. There is no sixth command needed this weekend — deliberately scoped for people who have not used git in a team.

nodes.label: Rules That Are Not Negotiable
nodes.rationale: No force push, no model files committed (.task/.onnx/.tflite live in models/ behind .gitignore), only push code that builds, pull before you push.

nodes.label: Conflict Escape Hatch
nodes.rationale: Copy the file somewhere safe, delete the folder, clone fresh, paste back, commit and push. It feels crude, takes four minutes, and has never once made things worse.

nodes.label: Tonight Setup Checklist
nodes.source_location: Part Two, 'Tonight, all three of you'
nodes.rationale: git config name/email, clone, open in Android Studio and press Build — tonight, not tomorrow, while there is still time and internet to fix a machine that cannot build.

nodes.label: Red Light Build Constraint
nodes.rationale: Roughly 10.5 hours where nobody can compile; the exact rule must be confirmed at the Saturday teach-in because the whole schedule depends on the answer.

nodes.label: Green Compile Windows
nodes.rationale: Sat 11:00-13:00, Sat 15:30-16:30, Sun 01:00-06:30. Do not spend a Green window on anything doable during Red Light.

nodes.label: Kshitij Desai (Team Guide)
nodes.rationale: The spine — everything the product actually does. Tonight: get it building, twelve tests passing, push, and start the ~3 GB Gemma 3n download early because it sits behind a Hugging Face licence acceptance.

nodes.label: Anushka Unde (Team Guide)
nodes.rationale: Everything the judge touches. Column, Row, Box, Text, Button, Modifier and remember are genuinely enough to build all four screens; during Red blocks she designs and sketches so she can type the moment Green opens.

nodes.label: Ayaan Memon (Team Guide)
nodes.rationale: Kshitij writes the code, Anushka makes it look right, Ayaan makes sure there is something to show and someone who can explain it. Neither coder will have time for any of it.

nodes.label: Scoring Categories
nodes.rationale: Office Kit usage 10% (HackTracker device data, not self-reported), demo and presentation 10% (human-judged 3-5 minute pitch), end product quality 30% (2.5-minute live demo).

nodes.label: Office Kit Usage Log
nodes.rationale: Plain text, one line per use in docs/officekit-log.md. Two reasons: evidence for the 10%, and it feeds straight into the technical document. Make it a reflex from hour one.

nodes.label: Check-In Tasks
nodes.source_location: Part Three, 'At check-in, three things only you do'
nodes.rationale: Enable developer options and USB debugging — on iQOO the second toggle 'USB debugging (security settings)' usually needs a vivo account sign-in, so do it while there is still network or nobody can install anything all weekend. Pair Office Kit and confirm all four functions. Ask the organisers out loud whether the laptop may compile during Red Light.

nodes.label: Hour-by-Hour Schedule
nodes.rationale: Saturday check-in through Sunday Eval 2, including Eval 1 at 19:00-22:00 (scored, and the whole value is finding out what confuses people) and Sun 06:30-09:00 recording five real guides, running the demo in airplane mode three times, and breaking it on purpose — cover the mic, move the phone mid-step, make the room loud.

nodes.label: Pitch Structure (Team Guide)
nodes.source_location: Part Three, 'The pitch, and the log'
nodes.rationale: Five beats, same shape every time. Do not cut point four — stating limits reads as more credible, and technical judges notice immediately.

nodes.label: Deck Visual Language
nodes.source_location: Part Three, 'Carry the deck into the app'
nodes.rationale: Paper background, black display type, blue accents — reuse it so the slides and the product look like the same thing.

nodes.label: Weekend Rhythms
nodes.rationale: Decide compile targets out loud 15 minutes before each Green window; four-hourly demo reality check; whoever is not blocked helps whoever is; sleep in shifts. There is no such thing as waiting on a three-person team.

nodes.label: Core Systems Role
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: Owns pure decision logic, hardware capture and on-disk storage because this is the part of ShowHow that must be provably correct without a phone in hand; keeping it separate is what makes the whole decision layer JVM-testable in milliseconds.

nodes.label: Core Imports Zero Android
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: core/ takes an onError callback the way PolicyStore does and lets data/ supply the Android side, so the fan-noise room stays a millisecond-long JVM test instead of needing a device.

nodes.label: No Magic Numbers
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: Every threshold, coefficient, duration and cap must exist as a field on core/Policy.kt with a default and a matching key in assets/policy.json, otherwise the change is unusable during Red Light when nobody can compile.

nodes.label: Cutter Stays A Pause Detector Plus Word List
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: If a fix seems to need a model, it is the wrong fix — a pause detector plus a word list runs in milliseconds on a five-year-old phone, which is the target hardware.
nodes.norm_label: cutter stays a pause detector plus word list

nodes.label: Mode Engine Stays A Decision Table
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: Four booleans, hysteresis and a dwell, deciding well inside 10 ms — asserted by ModeEngineTest; anything heavier cannot run per-frame on the target phone.
nodes.norm_label: mode engine stays a decision table

nodes.label: Degenerate Input Never Crashes
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: -Infinity from a dead mic, NaN from a divide-by-zero, empty sample lists, zero-length takes, truncated WAVs and stray policy.json keys each already have a test, because a demo cannot survive a crash on stage.

nodes.label: Nothing Blocks In Core
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: No API in the decision layer returns 'not allowed'; it emits advisory numbers only, so the product never refuses a user based on something it cannot honestly measure.

nodes.label: Photo To Step Index Mismatch
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: Photos are named from live cut detection (shots++) while steps come from the final ranges after mergeShort and the maxSteps cap, so the two indices drift apart; named the highest-value fix in the repo. The ViewModel is shared ground, so the fix is a core/-side helper mapping snap timestamps to StepRanges.

nodes.label: Link Word Confirmation
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: LinkWordConfirmer should be wired into StepCutter now using policy.linkWords(guide.lang) even though it is a no-op until ASR lands, so the ASR landing becomes a body change rather than an API change.

nodes.label: Behaviour Sentence Test Names
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: Tests are named as sentences about behaviour (e.g. `a long utterance does not drag the floor up`) so a failing test name is itself the diagnosis.

nodes.label: Ponytail Shortcut Comment
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: A deliberate shortcut carries a `ponytail:` comment naming its ceiling and upgrade path, so intentional simplifications stay distinguishable from oversights.

nodes.label: Hardcoded Mode Inputs
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: speechUnclear and userFar are hardcoded false in ModeInputs, guide language is hardcoded "hi" in buildGuide (leaving linkWordsMr dead), and Step.warning is never set — each needs a real source before the feature is honest.

nodes.label: AI Integration Role
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: Replaces canned answers with real on-device models without changing a single call site above ai/; if landing a real model needs a change elsewhere, the design has slipped and the interface gets fixed instead.

nodes.label: AiStack Interface Contract
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: ai/Ai.kt defines Asr, Captioner, GestureSource and SceneCheck plus the AiStack bundle; ShowHowViewModel's `val ai: AiStack = fakeStack()` is the entire integration surface, so swapping real for fake stays one line.

nodes.label: Offline Or It Does Not Ship
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: No model may fetch anything: the manifest has no INTERNET permission and strips it at merge, so a library that needs the network to initialise is by definition the wrong library.
nodes.norm_label: offline or it does not ship

nodes.label: Models Never Enter Git
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: .task, .onnx, .tflite, .gguf and **/models/ are gitignored; models live on the phone and in Drive and move by Office Kit file transfer. If git status shows one, stop.

nodes.label: Missing Model Degrades To Fake
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: Every real implementation falls back to its fake (or an empty result) when the model file is absent and logs it once, because the demo must survive a phone that never received the file.

nodes.label: Models Get No Veto
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: SceneCheck returns a number and Asr returns words with confidences; the decision belongs to core/ and the answer to the user is always advice, never a block.

nodes.label: Keep The Fakes
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: Fakes.kt is how the app stays demoable and how anyone without a 3 GB download can run the project, so it is never deleted.

nodes.label: Models Never On The Main Thread
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: Everything model-shaped is expensive; use Dispatchers.Default/IO and honour cancellation the way AudioRecorder.record does.
nodes.norm_label: models never on the main thread

nodes.label: Vosk Speech Recognition
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: transcribe(wav) runs over the finished take.wav, which is already PCM16/16 kHz/mono — exactly what Vosk wants, and why the recorder writes its own WAV header. Unlocks LinkWordConfirmer, real step titles and speechUnclear from confidence.

nodes.label: MediaPipe Gesture Recognition
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: Recognise from the same ImageAnalysis stream as the scene check — one analyzer, not two — and somebody must actually collect the flow, since HANDS mode does nothing until the Player consumes it.

nodes.label: Gemma 3n Captions
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: ~3 GB behind a Hugging Face licence acceptance so the download starts first, but lowest priority: FakeCaptioner is convincing on stage and this is the most likely item to be cut for time.

nodes.label: Wiring RealSceneCheck Into ShowScreen
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: RealSceneCheck is written (dHash + HSV) but never called because ShowScreen binds the camera with analyzer = null. It is free — nothing to download — and demonstrates the whole on-device claim in one line of UI.

nodes.label: R8 Disabled On Purpose
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: R8 is off in release deliberately because it breaks MediaPipe, which stack-walks to load its native libraries. Do not re-enable it.

nodes.label: libc++_shared pickFirsts And arm64-v8a Only
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: All three ML libraries ship their own libc++_shared.so and the merger refuses to pick, hence pickFirsts in app/build.gradle.kts. Only arm64-v8a is built: the demo fleet is arm64 and four ABIs would triple an APK that only ever travels over USB.

nodes.label: UI Compose Role
nodes.author: Anushka
nodes.rationale: Owns every Compose screen, the theme and all visuals — everything the judge looks at — and nothing below ui/ and res/.

nodes.label: No Disabled Controls
nodes.author: Anushka
nodes.rationale: Warnings advise, they never block: a Step.warning or a low scene-check score is a line of text next to a button that still works.

nodes.label: The User Never Picks A Mode
nodes.author: Anushka
nodes.rationale: The phone reads the room and the UI reflects the decision; there is no mode selector, only the Easy Mode switch, which is a setting rather than a guess.
nodes.norm_label: the user never picks a mode

nodes.label: Always Show The Reason
nodes.author: Anushka
nodes.rationale: Every mode switch carries a human string like "HANDS <- room is loud (-24.3 dBFS)" in a reason bar pinned to the bottom of the Player: it is the honesty of the product made visible, and the jury notices.

nodes.label: Numbers Come From Policy
nodes.author: Anushka
nodes.rationale: Thresholds and timings come from vm.policy so they stay tunable without a compiler; spacing, type scale and colour belong to the UI role.

nodes.label: Debug Screen Content Is Load-Bearing
nodes.author: Anushka
nodes.rationale: The Debug screen may be restyled but nothing on it is removed — every number on it is load-bearing at 3 am when the only diagnostic available is what the phone prints.

nodes.label: Sealed Interface Navigation
nodes.source_location: What you already have to work with
nodes.author: Anushka
nodes.rationale: Navigation is a sealed interface plus a `when` in ShowHowHost.kt, because Navigation-Compose buys nothing for five screens and costs an argument about routes at 2 am.

nodes.label: ViewModel StateFlow Surface
nodes.source_location: What you already have to work with
nodes.author: Anushka
nodes.rationale: Screens collect screen, debug (DebugState: levelDb, gateDb, floorDb, accelVariance, mode, reason, switches, recording, elapsedMs, samples, liveCuts, policyError), library, easyMode and policy with collectAsStateWithLifecycle. If a screen needs data the ViewModel does not expose, ask rather than adding it.

nodes.label: Four Player Visual States
nodes.author: Anushka
nodes.rationale: TAP (held phone, quiet room), TALK (phone flat or user far — huge type legible across a room, one instruction at a time), HANDS (loud room or unclear speech — usable with no touching at all), EASY (user override, simplest layout), plus the reason bar.

nodes.label: Paper Black Blue Visual Language
nodes.author: Anushka
nodes.rationale: Paper background, black display type, blue accents carries the deck into the app so the slides and the product read as the same thing. Theme.kt is deliberately stock Material 3 and replacing it is this role's call.

nodes.label: Policy Tuning Role
nodes.author: Ayaan
nodes.rationale: Changes how the app behaves without a compiler, which for ~10.5 hours of the event is the only kind of change anyone can make. Values only — adding or renaming a key is a Kotlin change owned by core-systems.

nodes.label: Red Light Window
nodes.author: Ayaan
nodes.rationale: For roughly 10.5 hours of the event nobody can compile, so the entire design pushes tunables out of Kotlin into policy.json and asks UI work to be sketched ahead and pasted the moment a Green window opens.

nodes.label: Policy Hot Reload
nodes.source_location: How a change reaches the phone
nodes.author: Ayaan
nodes.rationale: adb push to /data/local/tmp then run-as copy into files/policy.json; the app watches the directory and reloads instantly — no restart, no rebuild, which is what makes tuning possible during Red Light.

nodes.label: Seed Asset Versus Phone Copy
nodes.source_location: How a change reaches the phone
nodes.author: Ayaan
nodes.rationale: The repo asset is the seed only: copied once on first run, after which the phone reads its own copy. Editing the repo file changes what a fresh install starts with; pushing changes what this phone does now — do both or a good value is lost at the next reinstall.

nodes.label: Malformed Policy Is Ignored
nodes.source_location: How a change reaches the phone
nodes.author: Ayaan
nodes.rationale: A malformed file is logged and ignored and the last good values stay in force, so a typo costs nothing — but the Debug screen prints the parse error and every live value, so check it. Unknown keys are silently ignored (ignoreUnknownKeys = true).

nodes.label: Gate Knobs
nodes.author: Ayaan
nodes.rationale: gateFallCoef 0.25 falls fast on purpose (0 to a -20 dB fan in about half a second), gateRiseCoef 0.004 creeps back slowly so a long sentence cannot drag the floor along, speechMarginDb 9.0 is the main sensitivity dial, and gateMinDb/gateMaxDb -45/-6 hard-clamp the threshold.

nodes.label: Cutter Knobs
nodes.author: Ayaan
nodes.rationale: pauseMs 1200 is the main step-count dial, minUtteranceMs 2500 merges anything shorter into the following step, maxSteps 12 is a hard cap with the remainder landing in the final step.

nodes.label: Mode Engine Hysteresis Knobs
nodes.author: Ayaan
nodes.rationale: inHandEnterVar/inHandExitVar 0.09/0.05 and roomLoudEnterDb/roomLoudExitDb -26/-32 keep enter and exit apart so a value sitting on the line cannot flicker; dwellMs 400 makes a candidate mode survive before it is committed. Setting enter equal to exit removes the hysteresis and the demo starts flickering.

nodes.label: Hindi And Marathi Linking Word Lists
nodes.author: Ayaan
nodes.rationale: linkWordsHi and linkWordsMr capture how a person says "and now the next thing" (phir, ab, uske baad, next, then / mag, ata, tyanantar, next, then), aiming at 15-20 Hindi and 10 Marathi, gathered by asking real people at the venue to explain a process out loud. Lowercase, no punctuation, multi-word phrases allowed.
nodes.norm_label: hindi and marathi linking word lists

nodes.label: Symptom To Knob Table
nodes.author: Ayaan
nodes.rationale: Maps an observed phone symptom straight to the knob that fixes it — one enormous step means speechMarginDb or pauseMs down, too many tiny steps means pauseMs/minUtteranceMs up, mode flipping on stage means dwellMs up and a wider enter/exit gap — so tuning under stage pressure needs no reasoning from first principles.

nodes.label: One Number At A Time Method
nodes.author: Ayaan
nodes.rationale: Change one number, push, watch the Debug screen, record what happened, and keep a numbered trail (policy.json v4) in the Office Kit log so a good value survives a bad one. If two changes go over together and behaviour improves, you have learned nothing.
nodes.norm_label: one number at a time method

nodes.label: Demo Pitch Role
nodes.author: Ayaan
nodes.rationale: Exists because two scoring categories worth 20% belong to nobody else while the other two people write code until the last hour; it also protects the 30% product-quality score judged on a live demo.

nodes.label: Hackathon Scoring Categories
nodes.author: Ayaan
nodes.rationale: Office Kit usage 10% judged on HackTracker device data (cannot be faked on Sunday morning), demo and presentation 10% judged by humans over a 3-5 minute pitch, end product quality 30% judged on a 2.5-minute live demo — so a fumbled recording on stage takes the 30% with it.

nodes.label: Office Kit Usage Log
nodes.author: Ayaan
nodes.rationale: Plain text, one line per use, from hour one: steady use across all 30 hours scores better than a burst at the end and feeds the technical document. Every model file and policy.json revision moves by file transfer rather than cable, and screen mirror stays on during debugging because it is genuinely useful and also counts.

nodes.label: Check-In Prerequisites
nodes.author: Ayaan
nodes.rationale: Enable developer options and USB debugging (the iQOO's second 'USB debugging (security settings)' toggle usually needs a vivo account sign-in, so do it while there is still network), pair Office Kit and confirm all four functions, and ask organisers out loud whether the laptop may compile and deploy during Red Light — the whole schedule depends on an answer from a person, not the website.

nodes.label: Demo Runbook
nodes.author: Ayaan
nodes.rationale: Numbered steps a stranger could follow, because on Sunday you will be tired: exact device state (airplane mode on, volume up, brightness up, guide preloaded), exact taps in order, the four-second no-INTERNET proof, and the fallback when something breaks mid-demo. Run it in airplane mode at least three times, timed, inside 2.5 minutes.

nodes.label: Break It On Purpose
nodes.author: Ayaan
nodes.rationale: Cover the mic, move the phone mid-step, make the room loud, put the phone flat: each should visibly change the mode and print a reason. That is the product working, not failing, and knowing it in advance turns a scary judge question into the best moment of the pitch.

nodes.label: Five Recorded Guides
nodes.author: Ayaan
nodes.rationale: Recorded Sunday 06:30-09:00 as insurance for the 30% live-demo score, after practising with throwaway guides on Saturday night. A good guide is a real task with clear pauses between steps (the cutter is a pause detector, so the expert breathes rather than races), a stable phone, and a scene that looks different at each step.

nodes.label: The Five-Beat Pitch
nodes.author: Ayaan
nodes.rationale: Problem in one sentence, Show Mode, Guide Mode, the honest part, then the proof. Write a bad first draft early because editing something bad beats starting from blank, and say it out loud twenty times before the final round, not five.

nodes.label: The Honest Part
nodes.author: Ayaan
nodes.rationale: Never cut point four: say plainly what the product refuses to claim — gloves, driving, whether someone is elderly, whether the work is correct. Most teams do not have it, stating limits reads as more credible rather than less, and technical judges notice immediately. Anything the phone cannot honestly measure is a setting, not a guess.

nodes.label: No INTERNET Permission Proof
nodes.author: Ayaan
nodes.rationale: Opening Android app info and showing there is no INTERNET permission proves the offline claim in four seconds; airplane mode during the demo both proves it and removes every notification risk. A guide is a folder you can copy off the phone with a file manager, so the data goes nowhere.

nodes.label: Technical Answers For Judges
nodes.source_location: The technical answers to have ready
nodes.author: Ayaan
nodes.rationale: Why an adaptive gate and not a fixed threshold: a ceiling fan floors a room around -20 dBFS, so a gate nailed at -38 dB reads that as continuous speech, finds no pause, and the whole take returns one enormous step; instead the gate learns the room's floor, falling fast, rising slowly, and freezing during speech. Why no AI in the step cutter: a pause detector plus a word list runs on a five-year-old phone in milliseconds and a video model does not — the product is for workshops, not flagships. How the phone chooses a mode: four booleans and a decision table with hysteresis and a 400 ms dwell, every switch carrying its reason on screen. What it refuses to guess: gloves, driving, age, correctness.

nodes.label: Build Verify Role
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: Read-only gate before any push, before a Green window closes, and before a demo. It reports and hands findings to the role that owns the path rather than fixing, so verification never becomes another source of unreviewed change.

nodes.label: Verification Checklist
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: Seven checks run top to bottom, stopping at the first hard failure: tests, no-network permission, android-free core, no hardcoded tunables, nothing blocks, no enormous file about to be committed, and a full build when there is time.

nodes.label: Twenty-One JVM Tests
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: 21 tests across AdaptiveGateTest, ModeEngineTest, PolicyStoreTest, SceneHashTest and StepCutterTest, all of which must pass; report the failing test name because the names are sentences about behaviour, so the name is the diagnosis.

nodes.label: Merged Manifest Permission Check
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: Vosk, MediaPipe and ONNX all try to merge INTERNET in, so the merged manifest is re-grepped after every dependency change; exactly CAMERA and RECORD_AUDIO are expected, and INTERNET, ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE or WAKE_LOCK surviving the tools:node="remove" strip is a stop-everything finding.

nodes.label: Android-Free Core Check
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: grep -rn '^import android' over core/ must print nothing: core/ being android-free is what keeps the whole decision layer JVM-testable in seconds instead of needing a phone.

nodes.label: Tunable Drift Check
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: Every field in core/Policy.kt should have a matching key in assets/policy.json and nothing in core/ should compare against a literal threshold — a drifted default is invisible until the team tries to tune it during Red Light and nothing happens.

nodes.label: Nothing Blocks Check
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: No `enabled = false` on any control and no code path that refuses to continue because a warning or score is low — warnings advise.

nodes.label: Model File Commit Check
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: A .task, .onnx, .tflite, .gguf or anything under models/ showing up in git status --short is a stop-everything finding, because they are gitignored and a survivor means the ignore was bypassed.

nodes.label: Pre-Demo Checks
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: Installs and launches on the actual phone, works fully in airplane mode, app info shows only Camera and Microphone, Record -> Review -> Play round-trips with photos on the right steps and "Hear it" playing the right slice, the Debug screen shows a live level and a tracking floor and a readable mode change, and the demo fits 2.5 minutes timed.

nodes.label: Ranked Finding Report Format
nodes.author: Kshitij
nodes.rationale: Most severe first, each as file:line - what is wrong - what it breaks - the smallest fix. Nothing is fixed by this role, a passed check is said plainly, a skipped check is never reported as passed, and findings already tracked in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §10 are noted as still-present rather than re-reported as new.

nodes.label: Core Systems Stub
nodes.rationale: Thin Claude Code agent stub: points at AGENTS.md and agents/core-systems.md and restates only the non-negotiables (android-free core, every number in Policy.kt and policy.json, cutter stays a pause detector, green tests).

nodes.label: AI Integration Stub
nodes.rationale: Thin Claude Code agent stub pointing at agents/ai-integration.md; restates offline-only, no models in git, degrade to fakes, keep Fakes.kt, one-line swap in ShowHowViewModel.

nodes.label: UI Compose Stub
nodes.rationale: Thin Claude Code agent stub pointing at agents/ui-compose.md and ARCHITECTURE.md §9; restates no disabled controls, no mode picker, policy-driven numbers, Debug screen untouched.

nodes.label: Policy Tuning Stub
nodes.rationale: Thin Claude Code agent stub pointing at AGENTS.md §7 and agents/policy-tuning.md; restates values-only, one number at a time, enter/exit apart, both copies updated, never open a .kt file.

nodes.label: Demo Pitch Stub
nodes.rationale: Thin Claude Code agent stub pointing at AGENTS.md, docs/WORKFLOW.md and agents/demo-pitch.md; restates keeping pitch point four, airplane-mode 2.5-minute demo, the no-INTERNET proof, and logging Office Kit use from hour one.

nodes.label: Build Verify Stub
nodes.rationale: Thin Claude Code agent stub pointing at agents/build-verify.md; restates read-only reporting, ranked file:line findings handed to the owning role, and never reporting a skipped check as passed.
